summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of ITR-U, but some key details regarding the filing timeframe and additional tax rates are outdated due to recent budget amendments.

claims.claim: Taxpayers can file an ITR-U within two years from the end of the relevant assessment year.
claims.note: The time limit for filing ITR-U has been extended to four years (48 months) from the end of the relevant assessment year, effective from April 2025 (Budget 2025).

claims.claim: Filing an ITR-U requires paying an additional tax of 25% or 50% on the extra tax liability, depending on when it's filed.
claims.note: While 25% and 50% rates apply for filings within 12 and 24 months respectively, additional tiers of 60% (within 36 months) and 70% (within 48 months) have been introduced with the extension of the filing window.

claims.claim: This mechanism cannot be used to reduce taxable income, claim a refund, or increase a loss carried forward.
claims.note: ITR-U cannot be filed to reduce tax liability, increase a refund, or increase a loss.

claims.claim: ITR-U is governed by Section 139(8A) of the Income Tax Act, which permits taxpayers to furnish an updated return.
claims.note: ITR-U was introduced under Section 139(8A) of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: If a search has been initiated under Section 132 or a survey under Section 133A, or if a notice has been issued for assessment/reassessment, or if prosecution proceedings have been initiated for the relevant assessment year, then an ITR-U cannot be filed.
claims.note: ITR-U cannot be filed if a search under Section 132 or a survey under Section 133A has been initiated, or if assessment/reassessment/revision/re-computation proceedings are pending or completed, or if prosecution proceedings have been initiated.

claims.claim: All payments must be made using Challan No. ITNS 280, selecting "Tax on Updated Return" as the type of payment.
claims.note: Challan ITNS 280 is used for income tax payments, including self-assessment tax, advance tax, and regular assessment tax. While 'Tax on Updated Return' is a specific category, it falls under the broader use of Challan 280.

article_title: Clearing Your ITR Backlog with the Updated Return (ITR-U)
